traumavision.label: Thesis · UNC Córdoba · 2026
traumavision.title: TraumaVision AI
traumavision.subtitle: Clinical Decision Support for Pediatric Wrist Fractures on X-Rays
traumavision.description: Academic prototype, built end to end: a YOLOv8m detector and a FastAPI web app with PDF reports. Held-out test of 3,038 images: 96.7% sensitivity, 93.1% specificity. External test without retraining: 97.4% / 88.3%. Now scaling through Emprende U 2026; next: more anatomical regions.

kibbo.eyebrow: Case Study · B2B SaaS · Built via Eleven · 2026
kibbo.title: KIBBO
kibbo.subtitle: A working hospital-equipment platform, and the website it never had.
kibbo.problem: KIBBO is a management platform (CMMS) for hospital medical equipment. The product worked, but kibbo.io still ran an old WordPress site that didn't explain it and throttled search crawlers. A biomedical engineer had nowhere to understand KIBBO, see it running, or check who already uses it.
kibbo.role: Through Eleven, I led design, front-end development, SEO/GEO and the English edition. The build ran on our AI-agent pipeline, with my review and sign-off at every checkpoint.

decisions.title: Write to the technician, not the buyer.
decisions.body: Third person, no hype, every claim shown on a real product screen, because the reader is the one who will run it every day.

decisions.title: Keep KIBBO and LEEX apart.
decisions.body: The hardware maker's figures are credited to LEEX, so KIBBO stands as its own product and never claims what it can't back.

decisions.title: Give mobile its own system.
decisions.body: "Expediente" reads each page like a case file instead of squeezing the desktop scroll into a phone.

decisions.title: Make English a real edition.
decisions.body: Own slugs, reciprocal hreflang and an untouched Spanish canonical; user quotes stay verbatim in Spanish with a labelled translation, so no one is misquoted.

kibbo.result: Live on kibbo.io in Spanish and English, replacing the legacy WordPress site, with GA4 measuring from launch.

Reciprocal ES/EN hreflang, x-default and a canonical per language.
Sitemap built from one route registry, dated by real edits.
Citable guides: CMMS explainer, tender checklist, country records (ES).

leex.eyebrow: Case Study · Internal B2B System · LEEX · 2026
leex.title: LEEX Tender System
leex.subtitle: Finds public tenders across 33 sources and helps sales decide which to bid on.
leex.problem: LEEX, an Argentine medical equipment company, sells mainly through public tenders: demand isn't generated, it's detected across dozens of government portals, each with its own format and deadlines. Seeing a tender late means never having it; seeing it without knowing whether you qualify means losing it. The previous tool was a single-user script feeding a spreadsheet.
leex.role: I led it end to end: scoped it with sales and management, designed the architecture, and built the engine and web app with a pipeline of AI coding agents under my direction.

decisions.title: Code before AI.
decisions.body: A deterministic dictionary-plus-vector match filters first and an LLM judges only what survives, because that keeps it cheap, testable and explainable.

decisions.title: A person signs every verdict.
decisions.body: The model drafts a requirement-by-requirement case citing the tender and the product sheet, and sales decides, because a missed tender costs far more than a review.

decisions.title: Three sweep states, not two.
decisions.body: "Nothing there", "couldn't see" and "saw far less than usual", because the expensive failure is the silent one.

decisions.title: Public first.
decisions.body: The engine reads each portal's public view and logs in only as a documented last resort, which reduced credential exposure and let the build start without waiting on access.

leex.result: Running internally on real data: the first full pass went from sweep to triage to human-signed verdicts. Next step: onboarding the sales team.

b6_story.title: Where the incubator came from
b6_story.caption: In 1878, a Paris obstetrician had a zoo's poultry incubator adapted for newborns; premature mortality fell from 66% to 38% with controlled heat alone. That idea is now LEEX's B6.
b6_story.made_with: Made with: Claude Code · Remotion · React Three Fiber · faster-whisper · FFmpeg · CapCut — iPhone footage, Wellcome Collection engravings
b6_story.credit: Engravings: Wellcome Collection, via Wikimedia Commons · <license>CC BY 4.0</license> · cropped, color-treated, camera-animated.

kibbo_film.title: Preventive maintenance, from plan to execution
kibbo_film.caption: A maintenance plan takes a week to build, and the first unplanned failure pulls schedule and staff out of sync. KIBBO puts every preventive task in one filterable list the whole team can see.
kibbo_film.made_with: Made with: Claude Code · Remotion · faster-whisper · Python audio · FFmpeg · CapCut — iPhone footage, UI rebuilt in code

v8v_cpr.title: One-button CPR position
v8v_cpr.caption: How long does a hospital bed take to be ready for resuscitation? On LEEX's V8v electric bed, one button: press it and the bed lies fully flat, ready for CPR.
v8v_cpr.made_with: Made with: Claude Code · Remotion · faster-whisper · Python-synthesized SFX · FFmpeg — iPhone footage, Mixkit music

mri_explainer.title: How an MRI works
mri_explainer.caption: No cameras, no X-rays: the body is full of water, and each hydrogen nucleus behaves like a tiny magnet. A strong magnet, a radio pulse tuned to their frequency and gradient coils turn that signal into an image. Not a photograph: the hydrogen in the body, made visible.
